_doc: Pinned evaluation set for work/2026-08-08-direction-consistency.
Every change to the pipeline is measured on THESE cells so two runs are comparable.
Mirrors bin/lib/eval_set.json, which does the same job for the LoRA harness.
WHY THESE SUBJECTS. Each answers a different question, so a change that helps one and
breaks another is visible rather than averaged away:
wolf     - the incumbent. Every prior sheet in this project is a wolf, and it is the only
subject with a measured baseline (spread 24.9 on 2026-08-08).
bear     - a quadruped whose corpus value sits at the DARK end. Our failure is being too
pale, so a dark subject is where the absolute-value gap should hurt most.
fox      - the corpus's most SATURATED animal (Fox_Red sat 70.2 against a grey wolf's
10.6-17.5). Saturation collapse is defect three; this is the cell that shows it.
anteater - NO corpus analogue. Carried forward from the predecessor's generalisation test.
A pipeline that only holds identity on animals the LoRA has seen is not a
pipeline, and this is the honest check.
WHY THESE SEEDS. Three, fixed. The predecessor measured two identical training runs differing
by 17.31/255 mean, and the six-seed sweeps showed seed dominates north/south outcomes - so a
one-seed verdict is noise. Three is the smallest number that shows a spread is not a fluke.
WHY cn/cn_end/strength ARE HERE and not CLI defaults. forks.md F3 floors cn at 0.5: lowering
it closes the metric by destroying the silhouette (the cn 0.2 featureless-slab result). Pinning
it in the file makes a change to it a visible diff rather than a forgotten flag.
The CEILING is measured off the real corpus, not chosen - three views of one animal sit within
9.0 luminance. See README.md.

subjects.why: the incumbent; the only subject with a measured baseline
dark-end corpus value; where the too-pale gap should hurt most
the corpus's most saturated animal; shows saturation collapse
no corpus analogue; the honest generalisation check

_template_note: Every subject reads the WOLF template triple. That is deliberate and it is a LIMIT, recorded
rather than hidden: the pipeline is template-driven (I4), only quadruped templates exist
today, and swapping templates per subject would change the silhouette between cells and make
the interior numbers incomparable. So this set measures CONSISTENCY, not species fidelity -
the bear and the anteater come out wolf-shaped, and that is fine for the question being asked.
A per-body-plan template library is the sprite-gen plan's reference library and is not this
